title: German Federal Environmental Foundation (DBU): PhD Scholarship Programme
summary: DBU PhD scholarships support junior researchers carrying out doctoral theses addressing environmental protection or nature conservation issues in Germany.

degree_levels.notes: Doctoral studies will take place at a German university and have not yet started.

subject_areas.notes: Applications are welcome from all disciplines, especially interdisciplinary environmental research.

nationality.notes: German and foreign nationals admitted to postgraduate studies at a German institution of higher education. A large list of countries is shown in the selection dropdown.

residence.notes: Work must be carried out predominantly in Germany.

mandatory.text: above-average degree (overall grade at least good or very good; law: at least fully satisfactory)
doctoral studies will take place at a German university and have not yet started
project not started if applicants have scientifically dealt with the topic for more than 1 year since graduating
good knowledge of German (at minimum B2 level)
doctoral thesis clearly addressing relevant environmental protection or nature conservation issues

funding.description: base amount of 1,650 EUR per month; fixed allowance of 150 EUR per month for material expenses and travel; further contributions to material expenses possible; subsidy towards health insurance of up to 150 EUR possible; additional support for fellows with children
funding.duration: Maximum funding covers a period of 3 years.

application_rounds.notes: Application deadlines are 15 January and 15 June of each year.
Application deadlines are 15 January and 15 June of each year.

recurring_deadline_notes: Application deadlines are 15 January and 15 June of each year.

steps.text: Use the application portal on a desktop computer.

sources.title: German Federal Environmental Foundation (DBU): PhD Scholarship Programme - DAAD - Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst
sources.notes: International and German doctoral students can receive funding for carrying out doctoral theses predominantly in Germany.
